subject: Pilot pricing & unit-econ check — token volumes and benchmarking
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@acmehealth.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up — pilot pricing & usage profile

Hey Hannah — great demo this morning. A quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can move to legal/SOW quickly.

Use case recap (high level):
- In-product summarization + structured extraction for claims processing (NLP pipeline that hits model for 1–2 short prompts per transaction).
- Expected steady-state volume: 120M tokens/mo in Q3 if pilot converts. Peak bursts to ~350M tokens/day during batch reprocessing.
- Latency sensitivity: 95th percentile target < 400ms for short prompts.

Budget/goal: Our procurement lead flagged ~$10k–$25k/mo for the pilot phase, which maps to roughly $8–$20 per 1M tokens depending on how you map tokens to transaction cost. We need a clear $/1M token understanding (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and a simple comparison to the big hosts for internal approval (OpenAI, Anthropic, and any common open-host providers).

Can you: 1) confirm a target $/1M for a short pilot (30–60 days) with the volumes above, 2) show a short comparison vs OpenAI/Anthropic/open hosts, and 3) flag any speed/latency tradeoffs we should expect?

Also looped Jordan here for procurement. Attaching our internal usage profile.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Li
Head of Automation, Acme Health

Thanks Emma — great to meet you both. Quick recap + concrete next steps below so procurement has what they need.

Recap of what we heard:
- Workload: short prompts (few hundred tokens per call), high steady monthly token expectation (approx 120M/mo) with heavy daily burst windows for reprocessing.
- SLOs: 95p < 400ms (we can meet that on hosted and dedicated with correct routing/caching).

Pricing ask & clarifying Qs (so we size proposals correctly):
1) For the pilot, do you want a hosted (managed API) price or to evaluate Dedicated/Private options? Pilots often do hosted for speed-to-value.
2) Is the $10k–$25k/mo budget a hard limit for pilot spend or a target range that can accept a discounted pilot?
3) Will you be comfortable providing a small sample dataset for eval (we use this to validate latency/quality) — answer will affect caching and batch strategies.

Benchmark + initial target (attached): redwood-pilot-pricing-1m-breakdown.xlsx — this includes three straightforward options:
- Hosted (no commit): proposed pilot floor $18 / 1M tokens (applies to generation + extraction token mix we discussed).
- Hosted (pilot discount, 30–60d, no commit): $14 / 1M tokens (timeboxed pilot offer, limited burst capacity).
- Dedicated (monthly reserved capacity): evens out to ~$9–12 / 1M tokens at scale once committed (volume and commit-dependent).

Quick qualitative comparison vs public hosts:
- OpenAI: current list-tier tends to be higher for generation-heavy workloads; good latency but premium price.
- Anthropic: similar performance/price to OpenAI for chat-style flows; better safety/guardrails out of box for instruction-style tasks.
- Open-model hosts (varies): cheaper at scale when you self-host or use dedicated quantized runtimes; however, integration and ops cost can be material.

Tradeoffs: to hit your 95p <400ms we recommend Hosted+prefix caching for pilot. If the goal is lowest $/1M, Dedicated or Private with quantized models is the route but requires commit and some lead time for capacity.

Next steps I recommend:
- Hannah/Ben: produce a 2-page pilot SOW and baseline price (we aim to get that to you within 24 business hours).
- Emma/Jordan: confirm whether pilot should be hosted or dedicated and if procurement wants a capped spend pilot.
- Exchange a short sample (anonymized) for perf verification.

Attaching the pricing workbook for line-item clarity. Happy to hop on a 20 min call with Ben if procurement wants price breakdowns.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Quick note with practical benchmarking numbers from our pricing desk to help procurement map to competitors. Short table below (all numbers expressed as $ per 1M tokens and are illustrative for a short pilot):

Host / Option    | Typical pilot rate ($/1M)
----------------------------------
OpenAI (gpt-like managed)   | $22 – $30 / 1M
Anthropic (Claude-like)     | $20 – $28 / 1M
Common open-hosts (managed) | $16 – $22 / 1M
Redwood hosted (pilot discounted) | $14 / 1M (timeboxed 30–60d)
Redwood hosted (floor)             | $18 / 1M
Redwood dedicated (reserved @ scale) | $9 – $12 / 1M (commit-dependent)

Notes:
- The larger the commitment (3–12m), the easier it is to reach the dedicated pricing band — we can model a blended $/1M depending on expected monthly run rate.
- For your bursty reprocessing windows, dedicated capacity yields more predictable unit costs; hosted pilots are simpler to stand up but we throttle burst capacity unless reserved.
- We can also explore a capped pilot (e.g., $15k total spend cap) to match procurement constraints — that lets you validate latency/quality without open-ended spend.

If $10k–$25k/mo is the stated pilot budget, the $14 / 1M pilot-discounted hosted rate maps to ~714M tokens for $10k and ~1.8B tokens for $25k — so your stated Q3 steady-state (120M/mo) sits well under those ceilings, and bursts can be handled with a spend cap.

Happy to convert this into a one-pager for procurement with absolute ceilings and suggested SOW language.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
